headline: NRL Grand Final fever builds as Roosters meet Knights Sunday, while the RBA hikes rates to a 15-year high and Google drops its most powerful AI model yet.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara dropped 5.4% today — a rough session, though the broader lithium story isn't broken. News out of Nikkei Asia today flagged that Australian lithium miners are actually expanding and reopening as prices strengthen, which is a longer-term positive. Today's drop looks like short-term market noise rather than a change in fundamentals.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two slipped 2.2% last night. There's no major negative news — GTA 6 hype continues with new feature reveals (hurricanes, Red Dead-style hunting in Vice City). The dip appears to be general market softness rather than anything company-specific. Long-term GTA 6 thesis remains intact.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft gained 0.7% last night, buoyed by strong AI momentum. Reports of a 'trillion-dollar quarter' highlighted that Microsoft's AI trade shows no signs of slowing — Azure cloud and Copilot products continue to drive growth.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google dipped 0.6% last night despite launching its powerful new Gemini 4 Argon model — which actually beat OpenAI and Anthropic on benchmarks. The slight fall may reflect profit-taking or the fact the new model is in limited release only. The AI news is genuinely positive for the long-term thesis.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: No ASX price data available for today's close — VDHG didn't trade or data wasn't captured. Previous close was $76.50. As a diversified growth ETF, it broadly tracks global and Australian markets; no specific news today.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: No price data for today's session. Previous close was $94.57. Emerging markets exposure means VGE is worth watching alongside the AUD/USD rate, which slipped 0.6% today — a weaker Aussie dollar can modestly boost the AUD value of offshore holdings.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: No price data for today's close. Previous close was $539.12. US markets were roughly flat last night (S&P 500 barely moved), so no major moves expected when VTS next trades.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: No price data for today's session. Previous close was $17.14. The AI sector had a big news day — Google's Gemini 4 Argon launch and OpenAI's 'dots' agent announcement are both tailwinds for AI-focused ETFs like GXAI. Watch for a positive reaction when it next trades.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — big drop today, but hold firm
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals fell 5.4% today to $3.65, and you're now down about 46% on this position. That's painful. However, lithium prices are strengthening and Australian miners are reportedly expanding — the long-term thesis hasn't changed. For a buy-and-hold investor, selling here locks in losses right as the cycle may be turning. Sit tight unless your conviction in lithium has changed.

watch_today.title: MSFT — quiet outperformer, keep holding
watch_today.detail: Microsoft ticked up 0.7% last night and is now up over 16% on your position. The AI story — Azure, Copilot, and a 'trillion-dollar quarter' — keeps delivering. Nothing to do here except enjoy the ride. Strong hold for the long term.

watch_today.title: GOOG — Gemini 4 Argon is a big deal for the long-term thesis
watch_today.detail: Google dipped 0.6% last night despite unveiling Gemini 4 Argon, which beats OpenAI's GPT-6 and Anthropic's Claude on coding and reasoning benchmarks. The model is in limited release but Google's official blog confirms it's their most capable model yet. The short-term dip is noise — this is a long-term positive for Alphabet's AI position. Hold confidently.

watch_today.title: TTWO — down but GTA 6 hype alive
watch_today.detail: Take-Two fell 2.2% last night with no bad company news. GTA 6 feature reveals continue (hurricanes, legendary hunts), keeping the hype cycle going. You're down about 12.6% overall, but the GTA 6 launch catalyst is still ahead of you. Hold for now — selling before the biggest game launch in history would be premature.

watch_today.title: RBA rate hike — watch the impact on your mortgage and spending power
watch_today.detail: The RBA lifted the cash rate to its highest level since 2011 yesterday, and all four big banks have already passed the increase on to home loan customers. This squeezes household budgets and can slow the economy — worth factoring into any personal financial planning, especially if you have a variable-rate mortgage.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — AI sector had a massive news day, watch for a bounce
watch_today.detail: No price data today for your AI ETF, but the sector had huge news: Google launched Gemini 4 Argon (benchmark leader over OpenAI and Anthropic) and OpenAI launched its 'dots' personal AI agent. Both are bullish signals for AI stocks broadly. Keep an eye on GXAI when it next trades — could see a lift.

world.summary: A big day globally: US election integrity concerns mount, the Middle East situation remains tense with vessel attacks and Iran-US diplomacy, and US forces have completed their withdrawal from Iraq after two decades.

stories.title: US forces exit Iraq after two decades, leaving a power vacuum
stories.why_it_matters: After more than 20 years, US military forces have formally withdrawn from Iraq — a historic end to a presence that began with the 2003 invasion. The big concern now is that the exit leaves a significant opening for Iran to expand its influence in the region. For everyday Australians, a more Iran-dominated Middle East affects oil supply routes and geopolitical stability in a region the world relies on for energy.

stories.title: Vessel attacks resume in the Strait of Hormuz as Middle East crude exports partially recover
stories.why_it_matters: Ship attacks have resumed in the Strait of Hormuz — the narrow waterway through which a huge chunk of the world's oil passes — even as Middle East crude exports have recovered to about 80% of pre-war levels. This is directly relevant to oil prices: crude (WTI) jumped 1.5% last night to $91.79 a barrel. Sustained disruptions here could push petrol prices higher for Australian drivers.

stories.title: Iran indicates it has received a US response to its latest offer on ending the war
stories.why_it_matters: Iran says it has received an official US response to its latest proposal for ending the ongoing conflict — a sign that behind-the-scenes diplomacy is still happening. Any de-escalation in the Middle East would be a major positive for global oil prices and broader market stability. It's early days and nothing is resolved, but it's worth watching.

stories.title: Iran's currency hits a record low as war erodes economic stability
stories.why_it_matters: Iran's currency, the rial, has hit a new all-time low as the ongoing conflict continues to batter the country's economy. This kind of economic pressure can sometimes push governments towards diplomacy — or alternatively towards more aggressive behaviour. It's a sign of how much the war is costing Iran domestically, beyond just the military dimension.

stories.title: Trump officials abandon effort to investigate election threats as critics warn of 'conspiratorial attacks'
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration has reportedly shut down the federal effort to investigate threats to election infrastructure, while critics are warning that the White House is escalating 'conspiratorial attacks' — including on voting systems. Experts warn this leaves US elections more vulnerable to interference and undermines public trust. With the US being Australia's most important ally, American political instability has real ripple effects globally.

markets.summary: US markets were essentially flat last night — the S&P 500 barely moved (-0.02%) and the NASDAQ edged up 0.09%. Oil jumped 1.5% to $91.79 on Middle East tensions. Gold ticked up slightly. The Aussie dollar slipped 0.6% to 69.47 US cents. ASX 200 data wasn't available for today's close.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold nudging higher — investors keeping some safe-haven exposure amid global uncertainty.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar fell 0.6% — partly on RBA rate hike uncertainty. A weaker AUD makes your US holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO) worth slightly more in Aussie dollar terms.

politics.summary: The RBA has raised interest rates to the highest level since 2011, all four big banks have immediately passed on the increase, and debate is raging about whether the central bank is being too aggressive — including an awkward side-story about the RBA refusing to give its own staff a pay rise that keeps up with inflation.

stories.title: RBA hikes cash rate to highest level since 2011 — big banks pass it straight on
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank of Australia has lifted its cash rate (the rate it charges banks to borrow money overnight, which flows through to home loans and savings accounts) to a level not seen since 2011. All four major banks — CBA, NAB, ANZ, and Westpac — have already announced they're passing the full increase on to variable-rate mortgage holders. For anyone with a home loan, this means higher monthly repayments starting soon.

stories.title: Economists say let the RBA do its job — and stop the political blame game
stories.why_it_matters: Economist Saul Eslake has penned an opinion piece urging politicians to back off the RBA and let it control inflation without political interference. Both major parties have been publicly blaming each other — and the bank — for the cost-of-living squeeze. Eslake's argument: the RBA's job is to bring inflation down, and political noise makes that harder.

stories.title: RBA refuses to give its own staff a pay rise that keeps pace with inflation
stories.why_it_matters: In an awkward juxtaposition, the RBA — which just raised interest rates to fight inflation — has reportedly refused to give its own employees a pay rise that matches the inflation rate. Critics say this is hypocritical: the bank is asking Australians to tighten their belts while not doing so internally. It's unlikely to affect policy, but it's a PR headache for an institution already under political fire.

ai.summary: Massive AI news day: Google has launched Gemini 4 Argon, its most powerful model ever, claiming the top spot on benchmarks ahead of OpenAI and Anthropic. Meanwhile, OpenAI launched 'dots', a new personal AI agent. And separately, the US government's AI chatbot is avoiding answering questions about the 2020 election result.

stories.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Argon — beats GPT-6 and Claude at coding and reasoning
stories.why_it_matters: Google has unveiled Gemini 4 Argon after months of delays, and it's a big deal: the model claims the top spot on AI benchmarks ahead of OpenAI's GPT-6 and Anthropic's Claude, particularly in coding and reasoning tasks. The catch is it's currently in limited release — not yet available to everyone. This is directly relevant to your GOOG holding: it reinforces Google's position at the frontier of AI rather than falling behind competitors.

stories.title: OpenAI launches 'dots' — a personal AI agent 'built to handle everything'
stories.why_it_matters: OpenAI has launched 'dots', a personal AI assistant designed to handle everyday tasks autonomously — think scheduling, research, emails, and more, all in one place. Interestingly, OpenAI scrapped the launch of a separate new AI model over safety concerns before announcing dots. This is the next step beyond chatbots: an AI that doesn't just answer questions, but actually does things for you.

stories.title: US government's AI chatbot avoids questions about who won the 2020 election
stories.why_it_matters: The US government has launched an official AI chatbot, but it has been quietly updated to avoid debunking or contradicting Trump — including refusing to give a clear answer on who won the 2020 presidential election. Critics say this is a politicisation of a tool that should be neutral and factual. It raises serious questions about how AI is being used (or misused) by governments as a communication tool.

stories.title: Google restricts access to new AI model over safety concerns
stories.why_it_matters: Despite the fanfare around Gemini 4 Argon, Google is keeping it in limited release because of safety concerns — meaning it won't be widely available immediately. This is a recurring theme in frontier AI: the most powerful models get restricted while safety teams evaluate potential risks. It's a sign the industry is at least trying to be cautious, even if critics say it's not enough.

sport.summary: It's Grand Final week in the NRL with Roosters vs Knights at Accor Stadium on Sunday. Nathan Cleary has won the Dally M Medal for the season's best player. AFL coaching chaos continues with Chris Fagan leaving Brisbane after three straight premierships.

stories.title: NRL Grand Final: Roosters vs Knights — fever pitch ahead of Sunday's decider
stories.why_it_matters: The NRL Grand Final is on Sunday at Accor Stadium, with the Sydney Roosters taking on the Newcastle Knights at 6:30 PM. Knights fans are going berserk — Fox Sports reports Grand Final ticket allocations sold out in three minutes. The Johns brothers were reportedly moved to tears by the fan reception. It's shaping up to be one of the great Grand Final atmospheres.

stories.title: Knights Grand Final Early Mail: junior 'in the frame' for 90-year first; Roosters' Plan B revealed
stories.why_it_matters: The Grand Final early mail is out: a young Knights junior is reportedly in the frame to start, which would make history — something that hasn't happened in a GF for 90 years. On the other side, the Roosters have a 'Plan B' option being prepared by coach Trent Robinson ('Robbo'). Expect team lists to be the big talking point heading into the weekend.

stories.title: Nathan Cleary wins Dally M Medal — 'no worlds left to conquer'
stories.why_it_matters: Panthers halfback Nathan Cleary has won the Dally M Medal as the NRL's best player of the 2026 season — yet another individual honour for the game's dominant player of the era. The ABC's headline says it all: 'no worlds left to conquer.' Cleary's Panthers didn't make the Grand Final this year but he remains the benchmark player in the competition.

stories.title: Chris Fagan confirms Lions exit after three straight premierships
stories.why_it_matters: Brisbane Lions coach Chris Fagan has confirmed he will leave the club — an extraordinary end to one of the great AFL coaching stints. Fagan coached Brisbane to three consecutive premierships, which is an incredibly rare achievement in modern AFL. The Lions coaching job is now one of the most coveted positions in the game, with reports of five serious contenders already circling.

stories.title: AFL coaching merry-go-round: Roos assistant to interview, Geelong already hunting big names
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL coaching carousel is spinning fast. North Melbourne's assistant coach is reportedly set to interview for the top job, while five serious candidates are in contention for the Lions role. Meanwhile, Geelong are already on the hunt for big-name players for 2027 after missing out on Patrick Dangerfield's successor. The off-season is well and truly underway in the AFL.
